payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_session.py::test_an_edit_that_removes_nothing_is_refused_before_any_witness_reads_it stayed green with the spec's wrong version "The read's paths collected only from wrong versions, so the criterion probe's file is never read and its inert edit reaches the mutator." applied to saffron/cell/session.py as an edit. The claim was 'REVIEW refuses an inert edit before any cell applies it, for a criterion probe and a wrong version alike. `_apply_criterion_probes` takes the repo\'s declared inert patterns, which `_drive_cell` passes from `policy.probes.inert`. With a pattern declared, it reads the edited files with one `files_after` call. The call names the mirror, the spec\'s `tree_base`, the patch the critic cell applies and the set of files the edits name, criterion probes\' and wrong versions\' alike. A pair that names no edit is recorded `unproven` as at base, and its file is not read. A pair whose file reads as text, and whose edit `inert_edit` refuses under those patterns, is recorded `unproven`. Its reason is its `summary` and sits under `refusal`. It never reaches the mutator or a witness, so it is never `survived` and files no adequacy finding. The REVIEW line counts it among the refused. A pair whose file reads `None` reaches the mutator as at base, as does one whose `find` is absent from the text or occurs in it twice. The witness drives one cell of a stacked spec through REVIEW, under a policy declaring two inert patterns. Its `tree_base` differs from its `base_sha`. Its criterion-probe session names one inert edit on a third file the stubbed read returns as text. Its wrong-version session names five edits and one version it cannot express. They are an inert edit, an edit that keeps its find and adds a top-level statement that executes, and an inert-shaped edit on a file the stubbed read returns as `None`. The last two are inert-shaped edits whose find is absent from the text and whose find occurs in it twice. It asserts the read\'s arguments, the `tree_base` and exactly three files among them. It asserts the unexpressed version is recorded `unproven` with "this session named no edit". It asserts that only the last four reach the mutator. It asserts both inert edits\' records and the outcomes `unproven`, `survived`, then `killed` three times. It asserts that only the survivor reaches `rebuttal.json`, and both REVIEW lines\' counts.'. Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_saffron_gates.py::test_the_fast_gates_name_their_tool_and_pass_on_a_clean_tree[format], and the criterion's witness did not fail.
